item.title: German far-right's breakout moment? AfD party eyes outright win in regional election
item.description: Could Europeans awaken next Monday to another shock bellwether moment? German voters could for the first time since World War Two give an outright majority to a far-right party in regional elections. We’ll ask about the A-f-D’s push in Saxony-Anhalt and a charismatic lead candidate whose campaign strives to put charm above the vitriol usually associated with a party with pro-Nazi roots. Saxony-Anholt with a familiar tale: a former East German state rattled by globalization with declining industry and an aging population. Contrast its dying towns and villages with the dynamism of not-so-far… Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: US House passes bill to stop federal funding of universities boycotting Israel
item.description: The US House has approved a bill aimed at halting federal support for universities that boycott Israel, marking a significant political shift that now awaits Senate approval. The vote reflected a mostly partisan divide, with some Democrats voicing concerns about free speech implications. Amid escalating protests against Israel's actions in Gaza, supporters assert that the legislation addresses antisemitism, a claim contested by demonstrators who disagree with its intent. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Giorgia Meloni celebrates Italy’s longest-serving government since 1945
item.description: Italy's first female Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, has surpassed a longevity record set by the late Silvio Berlusconi. When she took office in 2022, many European allies viewed her with unease, given her party's neo-fascist roots. Yet she has governed pragmatically, working within EU institutions and even supporting Ukraine. Domestically, however, she has targeted same-sex parents and clamped down on press freedom. Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: Financial Times.

"Nuestro rol y relevancia en el mundo ha cambiado", aseguró el libertario, quien anunció medidas para hacer frente a la amenaza que representa el proyecto petrolero 'Sea Lion' para el reclamo argentino. item.title: Ben-Gvir propone desocupar Gaza de su población palestina antes de las elecciones en Israel
item.description: El ministro de Seguridad Nacional israelí de extrema derecha, Itamar Ben-Gvir, propone desocupar la Franja de Gaza de su población palestina, que sería enviada al extranjero, de cara a las elecciones legislativas del 27 de octubre. Ben-Gvir no nombró a ningún país dispuesto a acoger a los habitantes del enclave palestino. Según su plan, 250.000 palestinos se marcharían en el primer año y casi 1,86 millones al cabo de siete años. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Giorgia Meloni government becomes Italy's longest-lasting since World War II
item.description: Italy's first female Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, has surpassed a longevity record set by the late Silvio Berlusconi. When she took office in 2022, many European allies viewed her with unease, given her party's neo-fascist roots. Yet she has governed pragmatically, working within EU institutions and even supporting Ukraine. Domestically, however, she has targeted same-sex parents and clamped down on press freedom. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Putin habla de una paz “posible” en la invasión rusa a Ucrania, pero lo condiciona al cese de “amenazas” de Kiev
item.description: El presidente de Rusia, Vladímir Putin, aseguró este jueves 3 de septiembre que ve posibilidades para la firma de un "acuerdo de paz" con Ucrania, pero advirtió que estos esfuerzos se ven eclipsados por las amenazas de Kiev sobre el espacio aéreo ruso. Entretanto, Moscú anunció el cierre del Instituto Goethe, después de que Alemania informara de la clausura de la Casa de Rusia como represalia por el supuesto envío de explosivos al aeropuerto de Leipzig. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Informe desde Londres: Macron se reúne con el primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham
item.description: El presidente francés Emmanuel Macron se convierte en el líder internacional en reunirse con el primer ministro británico Andy Burnham, que lleva seis semanas en el cargo. En el encuentro destacaron temas como la guerra en Ucrania, la crisis migratoria en el continente europeo, la relación británica con la Unión Europea y, por su puesto, el Tapiz de Bayeux, que estará expuesto por un año en el Museo Británico. Nuestra corresponsal Luisa Pulido nos amplió la información. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spanish PM Sanchez says no evidence Morocco orchestrated Ceuta border surge
item.description: Spain has found no evidence to conclude that July's deadly border rush from Morocco into its enclave of Ceuta was orchestrated by Moroccan authorities, ​Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez ‌said on Thursday, countering allegations in a Spanish police report. Speaking in parliament, Sanchez responded to claims in ⁠the report that emerged this week suggesting the entry of over 70,000 people into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration but a planned effort to overwhelm border controls. Publicado también por: The Jerusalem Post - International. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Manchester synagogue attack: ministers seek to block MI5 files from inquest
item.description: Government lawyers tell coroner disclosing intelligence would pose serious risk to national security Ministers are seeking to block intelligence material from being heard at an inquest into the death of two men killed in the 2025 Manchester synagogue attack. Lawyers for Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, told a coroner on Thursday that disclosing the MI5 files would pose a serious risk to national security. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
